## What this notebook checks

Decide whether each clock-time outcome can be analysed on a linear scale using
the approved unwrapping rules, which express relevant pre-midnight nighttime
values as negative hours, or requires circular treatment, in which the end of
one day connects to the start of the next. Define the roles of the Munich
Chronotype Questionnaire (MCTQ) and Morningness--Eveningness Questionnaire
(MEQ). Account for site, photoperiod, repeated measurements from participants,
and days on which a timing metric cannot be calculated because the threshold
was not observed. Adjust each complete predefined group of \(p\)-values
together.

## What this notebook uses and produces

- Uses: the prepared H09 dataset in `artifacts/06_model_data/H09.rds`.
- Produces: the declared groups of timing tests, fitted models, model checks,
  adjusted estimates expressed as interpretable clock-time differences with
  95% confidence intervals, the exact participants, participant-days,
  observations, and sites used by each model. For each timing metric it also
  reports participant-days excluded because the threshold was not observed,
  temporal data support was insufficient, or another timing rule prevented
  calculation, with tables, figures, and source data.
- Data sensitivity: fit this identical H09 implementation to the
  manuscript-prepared dataset and compare exact samples, timing-unavailable
  reasons, estimates, 95% confidence intervals, diagnostics, and conclusions.
- Formula display: the completed audit must contain a visible evaluated code
  cell printing the exact Wilkinson formulas passed to the selected model and
  every fitted comparison model.
